checks: For an oblique normal with both components nonzero, multiply the cutting equation by a nonzero scalar to write the plane as z+t e·X=0. This changes raw coarea by a positive factor only, so vertical moment vanishing is equivalent to centroidal vertical centering.

The interval-mixture law has positive radii. Horizontal reflection makes M even in the slope. Thus M(|t|R) has the assumed strict sign for every radius, and its integrable average is nonzero. The centroid requirement excludes such a section.

A cap with zero vertical normal takes half of each centrally symmetric fiber. A cap with pure vertical normal uses z=0 with the same positive section area in either orientation. The vertical component of the weighted normal balance forces equal weights on those two orientations. Their volume fractions sum to one since the cutting plane is volume-null.

dependencies.hypotheses: D is centrally symmetric and the actual profile r is positive and concave on the prescribed interval. Its positive-radius mixture expresses the raw vertical first moment of a finite oblique normal (t e,1), divided by |D|, as the average of M(tR). Reflection permits |t|R. Centroid zero forces that moment to vanish.

overlap.comparison: Transfers the cap, raw coarea and vertical first moment from interval layers to an actual symmetric homothetic body. It does not state the strict-sign exclusion or the balanced cap mean.

Proves the same mean for an explicit double cone with zero axial endpoint radii, and excludes vertical cutting planes in its asymmetric case. This result is a strict-sign criterion for arbitrary positive profiles and also permits vertical cutting planes that are centroidal.

readability: A vertical normal gives the horizontal plane z=0. A normal with zero vertical component gives a vertical cutting plane. The balance concerns unit normals times their actual section areas.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: A strict sign of the finite positive-slope layer moment excludes all oblique centered sections. The remaining cap orientations have weighted mean one half.
